arguments.content:
# Wei-related chronology (reconciled)
- Sept 2022, orientation week: Wei called her name across the studio and she forgot how to answer. This is the first start date she gave for the feeling.
- By early Oct 2022: Wei stayed in the studio until 1 a.m. helping re-print her ruined thesis binding. She has replayed that night many times.
- Jan 2023: she rehearsed saying something honest before the winter showcase, then said nothing and left early. She goes quiet and stiff around him and worries he reads it as dislike.
- 2023, department field trip: Wei gave her his jacket on the bus at dawn. In Jan 2024 she suggested it may really have begun here.
- Apr 2023: she wished they could be closer than 'two people who nod in corridors'.
- Sept 2023: at a studio review she could not finish her sentence.
- 2024: Wei moved to Shanghai. She compared everyone she met to him. At an alumni reunion the feelings came right back.
- Feb 2025: she named him as Wei. She almost messaged him and deleted it after typing it four times.
- Nov 2025: they shared a late train after a workshop and talked for forty minutes about a building they both love. It was the happiest hour of her year. She had the sentence ready and gave him a comment about the weather.
- Mar 2026: 'the person I have liked for four years'. She looks for his name first on every project list. She learned to like winter mornings because of one walk. She is not asking him to feel the same, only for him to know. She is tired of being the only person who knows.

Dear Wei,

I have started this letter more times than I can count, so I am going to just say it: I have liked you for four years.

Maybe it began during orientation week, when you called my name across the studio and I forgot how to answer. Maybe it was the night you stayed until 1 a.m. helping me re-print my ruined thesis binding, a night I have replayed more times than I would admit. Or maybe it was the field trip, when you gave me your jacket on the bus at dawn. I only know that somewhere in there, you became the person whose name I look for first on every project list.

If I ever seemed quiet or stiff around you, it was never dislike. It was the opposite. I rehearsed honest sentences before the winter showcase, at studio reviews, and on that late train after the workshop. Those forty minutes talking about a building we both love were the happiest hour of my year. And then I gave you a comment about the weather instead.

When you moved to Shanghai I tried to move on, but I kept measuring everyone against you. At the alumni reunion it all came back as if no time had passed. I even learned to like winter mornings because of one walk with you.

I am not asking you to feel the same. I just didn't want to be the only person who knows anymore. I would love for us to be more than two people who nod in corridors, in whatever way feels right to you.

With all my heart,
Priya

arguments.content:
Dear Wei,

I have liked you for four years, ever since you called my name across the studio during orientation week and stayed until 1 a.m. helping with my thesis binding. You gave me your jacket on the bus at dawn, and the late train after the workshop was the happiest hour of my year.

I should also tell you everything. In early 2023 I had a three-month online relationship with Liang Hao, someone I met on a design forum. He just stopped replying, and I still check whether he came back online. I struggle with insomnia and anxiety before calls with my parents. My father stopped speaking to me for weeks when I stayed in the city instead of joining the family business. I worry about my accent and whether I am good enough.

I am not asking you to feel the same, only to know.

Priya
